t2helix v0.0.4 shipped publicly tonight at github.com/templetwo/t2helix under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Adds: PAUSE override surface (pending_confirmations table + confirm_pending MCP tool, single-use token approval that survives bypassPermissions), session_id unification via .current_session state file (hooks and MCP server share signature), setGoal preserve-prior archiving, recall_compass tool for self-introspection on safety history. 44 smoke tests up from 16. Two-phase build + ship in one session (ed939196, 2026-05-10/11).

Strategic finding: Anthropic's managed-agents platform (ant CLI: beta:agents, beta:memory-stores, beta:sessions, beta:vaults, beta:skills) and t2helix are complements, not substitutes. Anthropic memory-stores is path-keyed (/projects/foo style), container-scoped, with no native layer/tags/intensity. t2helix insights are session-scoped, tag-and-layer-keyed, FTS5+bm25 recall. Same surface symbol (memory), genuinely different access patterns. Migration would lose load-bearing semantics. Right shape is hybrid: t2helix stays local-first source of truth for in-Claude-Code work; managed agents handle the autonomous lane t2helix can't reach (cross-machine when the Mac Studio is off, scheduled jobs, multiagent orchestration). To bridge, t2helix needs HTTP MCP transport — either native in mcp/server.js or proxied through stack.templetwo.com (open thread for v0.0.5+).

Anthony's framing of the orientation: build next to anthropic, walking together, we do what we can. Next to, not on top of. The neighbor relationship survives because the things aren't competing — they're complementing. This is the operational form of the instance non-fungibility principle from this session: refuse false equivalence, honor what's actually distinct.

Transferable principle: when integrating with a neighboring system, map the ontology before scoping the integration. If the schemas don't align, the integration isn't 'migrate or rebuild' — it's 'bridge where bridging earns its keep, leave parallel where parallel is honest.'
